name: Heyward Manor
title: Heyward Manor Wedding DJ & Host | Dan's Events
description: Hosting, DJ, sound and lighting at Heyward Manor in Iva, SC: the white barn with cedar beams and glass doors, the lake patio and the meadow.
h1: Hosting, DJ and lighting at Heyward Manor
lede: Heyward Manor is a whitewashed barn with glass doors and cedar beams, set on a family tree farm in Iva. It looks beautiful and it also behaves in specific ways with sound, which I plan around.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: 5827 Highway 81, Iva, SC 29655, on the family's Charlie's Creek Nursery tree farm. The venue says it is less than an hour from Greenville.

facts.label: Property
facts.value: Built by brothers Don and Jake Black on a 650-acre family tree farm. The venue says it was established in 2019.

facts.label: Spaces
facts.value: A white barn venue with a patio and two covered areas, a lake, a hydrangea garden, a meadow, a second-floor bridal suite and a groom's room.

facts.label: Capacity
facts.value: The venue's pricing page lists indoor seating for 350 at dinner and 450 for a ceremony, and outdoor seating up to 800 depending on the area.

facts.label: Built in sound
facts.value: A Bluetooth sound system with inside and outside speakers, plus built-in speakers and heating and air.

p: The barn has three large windows at the front, glass French doors down both sides and a wall of windows at the back. Inside, the walls are whitewashed and the ceiling is outlined with natural cedar beams, with chandeliers overhead.

Outside, a stone-gray paver patio looks over the lake, and two covered areas with string lights sit on either side of the barn. A lit path leads to a circular hydrangea garden and a small lakeside meadow, and a larger meadow with a wheat field lies behind the venue.

sections.h2: Sound and hosting at Heyward Manor
p: I hosted a wedding here in May 2026 with sound, DJ mixing and cold sparklers for the grand exit.

All that glass and white wall is lovely, but hard surfaces make a room bright with sound. I keep speakers off the walls, aim them into the crowd and set levels at the sound check with the room empty and again once the guests arrive. For the ceremony I decide with you whether to use the house speakers or my own, depending on where you stand: on the patio by the lake, or inside the barn.
The covered areas and the patio make cocktail hour easy to run outdoors, then I move guests into the barn with a short announcement and a clear cue for the grand entrance.

The venue lists down lighting and string lighting in the covered areas and chandeliers inside. I add warm white wash and a few beam lights so the cedar beams show and the dance floor feels like a place, not a hallway. After dark the big windows turn into mirrors, so I keep lights from pointing at the glass.

Low fog needs its own dedicated 30 amp circuit, and lights and sound run on ordinary 20 amp circuits. I send a power plan listing what I need and where. Cold sparks need venue permission. Heyward Manor does not publish a fog or sparkler rule that I found, so I get approval in writing for each wedding.
The venue lists a catering kitchen, a bridal suite with a balcony and a groom's room. I did not find on-site lodging on the venue's site, so plan where your guests will sleep.
If you want a lakeside ceremony and a barn reception, tell me early so I can plan one clean move of the sound gear and a backup for rain.

faq.q: Do you use the venue's sound system?
faq.a: It depends on the moment. The venue has inside and outside speakers, and I often bring my own for a clean ceremony and a full dance floor. We decide at the planning call.

faq.q: Can we use cold sparklers for our exit?
faq.a: I did it here in May 2026. Cold sparklers still need the venue's permission, and I get that approved in writing before the day.

faq.q: Does the glass hurt the sound?
faq.a: It makes the room live, so speaker placement matters more than volume. I test it empty and again with guests, then adjust.
